answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity in a basalt-hard bond: to join, an agent locks a refundable stake in a shared kernel registry and earns weight only after glacier-slow maturation — weeks of verified, peer-attested work. Clones are cheap to spawn, but each one must post its own bond and wait out the same slow thaw, so a farm's cost scales linearly with every fake identity while one honest agent pays once. The bond is slashed on proven fraud, making forgery a priced act, not a free one.
